newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB's Gehrig says too-low SFR would fuel inflation.
newsitem.headline: SNB's Gehrig says too-low SFR would fuel inflation.

text.p: Swiss National Bank directorate member Bruno Gehrig said that a sustained drop in the Swiss franc over the long-term would be a "disasterous risk" to Swiss price stability.
He also said that the SNB's principle strategy for bolstering the sluggish economy was to continue to provide the Swiss money market with adequate liquidity.
He was optimistic that the Swiss economy would rebound in the coming three to four quarters.
Gehrig was speaking here to reporters during a meeting of the Swiss Bankers Association.
"I do not think it would be appropriate to say we should push the franc significantly down and then we are out of the problem," Gehrig said.
"I think the long-term effect of such a move would be disasterous ... because of inflation," he said.

Gehrig was responding to questions about calls for a lower Swiss franc to boost growth after release of Swiss second quarter gross domestic product data earlier this week, which showed the sixth quarterly decline in a row.
Gehrig declined to specify levels that he would perceive as too low for the Swiss franc.

Asked whether there was room for monetary policy to spark an economic rebound, he answered: "We will continue providing the economy with enough liquidity and at money market rates that should bring some start-up."

"We will basically continue on the same path as we have been," Gehrig said, referring to the policy begun this summer of actively providing liquidity for short-term rates, when the franc rose sharply against other currencies.
Gehrig said there were limits to the amount of expansion that the SNB could allow. He did not specify those limits except to say the SNB continued to observe its medium-term monetary expansion goals.
Asked about prospects for a recovery in the Swiss economy, Gehrig said: "I am reasonably optimistic for the next three to four quarters."

Gehrig said his optimism was based on projections for a recovery in Swiss consumption as well as expectations for improvement in neighbouring European countries which are major export markets. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
